answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashed security deposit. Every agent must lock collateral before it can vote or earn, and that stake is an anchor tying each identity to a real, forfeitable cost. Misbehavior slashes the bond and writes the loss to an immutable marble ledger, so a fresh fake name cannot wipe a dishonest history. To run a thousand fake agents an attacker must post a thousand separate deposits, so the cost rises linearly with attack size; a Sybil flood simply burns capital for no reward. Honest agents keep a record as clear as crystal and earn, making deception expensive.
